models.name: ai_mall_carts
models.description:
Shopping Cart entity - This implements the persistent multi-seller, cross-device cart requirement from the requirements document (see 04_ai-mall_cart-and-order-processing.md, 'Cart Management'). 

This model stores a customer's current shopping cart, supporting persistent and session-based cart recovery. Maintains 3NF compliance: only core atomic cart attributes are stored, with all related items separated into ai_mall_cart_items. For example, a user logs in from any device and retrieves a unique cart instance. 

Key relationships: One-to-many with {@link ai_mall_cart_items} (cart items), many-to-one with {@link ai_mall_customers} (cart owner, from Actors domain), and optional link to {@link ai_mall_cart_sessions} (enables device/session association). 
Special behaviors: Soft deletion via 'deleted_at', automatic restoration logic during login/session merge.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for the cart instance.

foreignFields.name: ai_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged customer's {@link ai_mall_customers.id}; identifies the cart owner. Implements cross-device and session merge logic.

foreignFields.name: ai_mall_cart_session_id
foreignFields.description: Optional link to shopping session {@link ai_mall_cart_sessions.id}. Used for session-persistent/guest carts before user login/merge. Nullable.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Cart creation timestamp - Implements audit/logging requirement. Represents when the cart was first created by the user or system. 3NF compliance: atomic event date only.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Cart last modified timestamp - Required for supporting auto-sync and concurrency control (e.g., real-time cart merging). 3NF compliance: captures only last update event.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp for recoverable cart deletion. Implements audit-log and logical delete without physical removal. Null if active.

models.name: ai_mall_cart_items
models.description:
Shopping Cart Item entity - This implements persistent, multi-product-item cart tracking, enabling dynamic update/merge logic per 04_ai-mall_cart-and-order-processing.md ('Cart Management', 'Real-time validation of inventory, dynamic pricing, and discount eligibility').

Stores precise entries for each product/variant in a cart. Maintains strict 3NF by storing only atomic item attributes; product/variant details are referenced, never duplicated. For example, each line in the cart—product + variant + quantity + pricing context—is an entry here.

Key relationships: Many-to-one with {@link ai_mall_carts} (cart header), references {@link ai_mall_products} and {@link ai_mall_product_variants} (from Products domain) for the selected product version, and links back to customers through the cart. 
Special behaviors: Supports atomic updates per item; does not cache pricing, stock, or totals (calculated at checkout/time-of-use).

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for a cart line item.

foreignFields.name: ai_mall_cart_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged cart's {@link ai_mall_carts.id}. Ensures item grouping to a specific persistent or session cart.

foreignFields.name: ai_mall_product_id
foreignFields.description: Product ({@link ai_mall_products.id}) added to the cart—foreign key to Products domain. Only atomic product id is tracked; all product details are externalized for 3NF.

foreignFields.name: ai_mall_product_variant_id
foreignFields.description: Product variant ({@link ai_mall_product_variants.id}) selected in cart. Implements fine-grained inventory and pricing per variant, never duplicated here (3NF).

plainFields.name: quantity
plainFields.description: Quantity of selected product/variant in the cart. 3NF: atomic count only. For example, 2 means 'user wants two of this variant'. Must be positive integer, enforced at application layer.

plainFields.name: added_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when item was first added to cart. For concurrency control and audit logs. 3NF: atomic event time.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when item was last updated (e.g., quantity changed). Supports multi-session merge, audit trail. 3NF: atomic update time only.

models.name: ai_mall_cart_sessions
models.description:
Cart Session entity - Implements the guest/anonymous shopping session persistence per requirements (04_ai-mall_cart-and-order-processing.md: 'Cart Management', 'Session resilience').

Tracks session-specific shopping carts for users who have not signed in, supporting cart restoration on reconnect/crash recovery. Maintains 3NF: atomic cart-session mapping only; all business logic occurs at application layer.

Key relationships: May be linked by {@link ai_mall_carts}, allowing a session cart to be merged into a user's cart on login (one-to-many or one-to-one depending on user flow).
Special behaviors: May be cleaned up on session expiry; soft-deleted via 'deleted_at'.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for the cart session.

plainFields.name: session_key
plainFields.description: Unique browser/device/session identifier, typically a secure random string or UUID. Used for mapping anonymous carts, preserving session state across reconnects. 3NF: atomic value only.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when session was created. Used for session lifecycle and audit.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this cart session was last used or modified. Enables cleanup and status tracking.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp. Null if session active. Implements safe lifecycle and recovery logic.

models.name: ai_mall_orders
models.description:
Order Entity - This implements the order tracking and management requirements from the requirements analysis (primarily from Cart & Order Processing and referenced in Promotions/Loyalty logic). 

This model records the core details of a transaction (customer, seller, order status, channel, timestamps). Maintains strict 3NF compliance: all item/product/fulfillment/payment detail is normalized into related tables. Example: a customer places an order spanning multiple sellers; each order instance is tracked here, referencing customer, channel, and initial status. 

Key relationships: Links to customer (Actors), seller (Actors), order status, channel (Systematic), and supports referencing payments and fulfillments. Special behaviors: immutable order_id, stateful via status referencing, all denormalized (summaries, counted totals) reside in separate materialized views only.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each order record.

foreignFields.name: ai_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged customer's {@link ai_mall_customers.id} - customer placing the order.

foreignFields.name: ai_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged seller's {@link ai_mall_sellers.id} - seller fulfilling this order split (multi-seller support).

foreignFields.name: ai_mall_channel_id
foreignFields.description: Related channel's {@link ai_mall_channels.id} - sales channel on which the order was placed.

foreignFields.name: ai_mall_order_status_id
foreignFields.description: Current order status {@link ai_mall_order_statuses.id} - points to order state (placed, paid, shipped, etc).

plainFields.name: external_order_code
plainFields.description: External Order Code - Implements third-party channel or system code assignment, used for reconciliation with partners/logistic systems. Normalization is kept by not duplicating core IDs, only allowing system-of-record pointers here. Example: Shopify order code.

plainFields.name: gift
plainFields.description: Gift Indicator - Implements requirement to track if order is a gift (special instructions on fulfillment/delivery). 3NF is maintained: related detail/notes handled via fulfillment or snapshot entities.

plainFields.name: buy_request_memo
plainFields.description: Customer Order Memo - Implements capturing of purchase comment/request. Normalized: only memo, not aggregation or status flags. Example: 'Please deliver after 6pm'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Order creation timestamp. Implements requirement for auditability and time-based querying. 3NF is kept by not storing derivative or summary values.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Order updated/modification timestamp.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp for audit/history compliance. Null if active.

models.name: ai_mall_order_items
models.description:
Order Item Entity - Implements the requirement to record normalized line item details for each order, per item/SKU, covering the structure outlined in Cart & Order Processing functional requirements. Strictly 3NF: product info/entity reference only, no denormalized rollups or calculations.

Business purpose: Each record is a unique product (and variant) ordered, with quantity, price, and per-item status. Example: Order containing 2 products generates 2 records here. Key relationships: links to ai_mall_orders, ai_mall_product_variants (Products), ai_mall_order_statuses. Special behaviors: separate status per item for partial fulfillment, references all by foreign key.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each order item.

foreignFields.name: ai_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to parent order's {@link ai_mall_orders.id}.

foreignFields.name: ai_mall_product_variant_id
foreignFields.description: Product variant SKU's {@link ai_mall_product_variants.id}.

foreignFields.name: ai_mall_order_status_id
foreignFields.description: Status of this order item {@link ai_mall_order_statuses.id}. Enables split fulfillment or returns per item.

plainFields.name: requested_quantity
plainFields.description: Quantity ordered - directly implements required per-SKU quantity tracking and normalization by separating item quantities to rows, not as aggregates. Example: 3 of SKU X, 2 of SKU Y across 2 rows.

plainFields.name: confirmed_price
plainFields.description: Confirmed Price - Business meaning: price per item (including discounts) set at the time of order item confirmation. Complies with 3NF as all calculations reside in reporting/materialized views.

plainFields.name: confirmed_currency
plainFields.description: Currency of confirmed_price (e.g., USD, KRW). 3NF: currency stored per item for multi-currency support without denormalization.

plainFields.name: product_title_snapshot
plainFields.description: Product Title at Time of Order - Implements audit-traceable ordering (snapshot pattern). Normalized: Stores only the business-facing title as it existed at order time.

models.name: ai_mall_order_statuses
models.description: Order Status Entity - Implements requirement for flexible, auditable order state tracking per order and per item. All business logic around order state transitions relies on these enumerations. Normalized: no aggregate or rollup data. Example: 'placed', 'paid', 'shipped', 'completed', 'cancelled', etc.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each order status.

plainFields.name: code
plainFields.description: Status Code - Short machine-friendly identifier (e.g., placed, paid, shipped, cancelled) supporting business rules. Normalization: Used by foreign-key reference, not duplicated in other tables.

plainFields.name: label
plainFields.description: Status Display Label (user-facing string) - Implements multi-language/locale friendly display. Normalized by keeping locale-specific data in separate translation/supporting tables.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Long-form business description for the status - implements audit and UI display requirements.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation timestamp, supporting audit/log requirements.

models.name: ai_mall_order_snapshots
models.description:
Order Snapshot Entity - Implements full audit-traceable and temporal storage for version history (requirement: snapshot pattern for order editing/auditing). Each record represents an immutable version of an order at a point in time. 3NF: no rollups, denormalized reporting, or calculated values here; only atomic snapshots at the time of update or significant event.

Business purpose: Enables rollback and change tracking. Example: changing shipping address triggers creation of a new snapshot. Links to parent order and stores who/what/when for inspections/audits.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each order snapshot.

foreignFields.name: ai_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: Parent order's {@link ai_mall_orders.id} - reference to the order whose state is snapshot.

foreignFields.name: ai_mall_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Reference admin actor's {@link ai_mall_admins.id} - identifies who/what made the order edit or override.

plainFields.name: snapshot_json
plainFields.description: Immutable JSON snapshot of the order state and details at this point in time. Normalization is maintained by not storing reporting/derived information, only the original state. Example: Change in fulfillment state, item list, or pricing structure all stamped atomically here.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Snapshot creation timestamp. Supports time-travel queries and audit logs.

plainFields.name: note
plainFields.description: Editor note, reason, or comment about why the snapshot was saved.

models.name: ai_mall_order_payments
models.description:
Order Payment Entity - Implements requirement from Payment Processing: stores individual payment events per order (cash/credit/point/etc), split payments, and refunds. 3NF: atomic payment events only, all aggregation handled in reporting.

Business purpose: Handles multiple payment attempts per order (installments, refunds), tracks method, amount, and status. Example: User pays half by card, half by points = 2 payment records. Key relationships: Links to ai_mall_orders, payment method, and admin (verified or managed by).

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each payment record.

foreignFields.name: ai_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to order's {@link ai_mall_orders.id} - the order being paid/refunded.

foreignFields.name: ai_mall_admin_id
foreignFields.description: If manually processed or confirmed, admin actor's {@link ai_mall_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: payment_method
plainFields.description: Payment Method Code - Implements business logic around payment types: card, cash, deposit, point, etc. Normalized: only short code, details in other structures or policies.

plainFields.name: paid_amount
plainFields.description: Exact paid amount for this payment event. Normalized: no aggregation or reporting fields.

plainFields.name: paid_currency
plainFields.description: Currency code for paid_amount (e.g., USD, KRW).

plainFields.name: payment_status
plainFields.description: Current status of payment (e.g., pending, completed, failed). May reference future status enum/extensions.

plainFields.name: payment_transaction_id
plainFields.description: External or gateway transaction reference ID.

plainFields.name: paid_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when payment was processed/received (atomic event).

plainFields.name: note
plainFields.description: Additional comment or admin note for this payment event.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Payment record creation timestamp for audit/tracing.

models.name: ai_mall_order_fulfillments
models.description:
Order Fulfillment Entity - Implements fulfillment tracking required for each order (shipping, delivery, pickup, etc). This is strictly normalized (3NF), with all summary data (e.g., delivery times, ship addresses) snapshotted for audit/history only.

Business purpose: Each record tracks one fulfillment event: outbound, return, partial, correction, etc. Supports multi-stage or split fulfillment. Example: 1 Order, 2 shipments. Key relationships: Links to ai_mall_orders, admin (actor), references external shipper/courier via external fields only.

foreignFields.name: ai_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: Parent order's {@link ai_mall_orders.id} - the order being fulfilled.

foreignFields.name: ai_mall_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Admin actor's {@link ai_mall_admins.id} if fulfillment was manually recorded or overseen.

plainFields.name: fulfillment_type
plainFields.description: Type of fulfillment event (e.g., shipping, in-store pickup, return, exchange).

plainFields.name: fulfilled_quantity
plainFields.description: Quantity fulfilled in this event (supports partial and staged fulfillments/returns).

plainFields.name: external_courier_code
plainFields.description: External courier or logistics provider code. Implements API/data exchange compliance without denormalizing shipment info in regular tables.

plainFields.name: tracking_number
plainFields.description: Package tracking number assigned by courier (for customer/state/reference).

plainFields.name: fulfilled_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when fulfillment was completed/carried out.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Fulfillment record's creation timestamp for audit/history purposes.

plainFields.name: memo
plainFields.description: Free-form comment, reason, or admin note for this fulfillment event.

models.name: ai_mall_order_fraud_flags
models.description:
Order Fraud Flag Entity - Implements the AI-driven fraud detection and manual override requirements from Cart & Order Processing and Analytics. 3NF is kept by storing each flag as a normalized record (not as aggregate or summary).

Business purpose: Each record is a fraud alert, risk score, or manual override for an order. Example: AI detects high risk; flag is set with score/status/reason. Key relationships: linked to ai_mall_orders, ai_mall_admins (if acted on), with timestamps and audit trail.

Special behaviors: Rigorous auditability. No denormalized metrics (counts/totals) are stored here – all reporting is handled externally or in mv_/analytics tables.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique fraud flag record.

foreignFields.name: ai_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: Order's {@link ai_mall_orders.id} that is suspected or flagged.

foreignFields.name: ai_mall_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Admin's {@link ai_mall_admins.id} if flag is set/acknowledged manually.

plainFields.name: flag_type
plainFields.description: Type of flag (e.g., ai_detected, manual, cleared, investigation).

plainFields.name: risk_score
plainFields.description: Numerical risk score assigned by AI or manual review. Normalization: calculated values or rollups are stored only in analytics, not here.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the fraud flag (e.g., active, resolved, dismissed).

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Textual reason or explanation why this flag was set (free-form or code references).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Flag record's creation timestamp for historical/audit compliance.

models.name: ai_mall_promotions
models.description: Promotion Campaigns - Implements core promotional campaign, sale event, and discount activities from the promotions and loyalty system documentation. Keeps campaigns atomic and normalized (3NF), supporting scheduling, activation, deactivation, and analytic tracing. This table has no calculated fields and is referenced by coupons. Example use: "Summer Sale" applied across listed categories.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each promotion campaign.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Title of the promotion event for user display. Example: 'Summer Sale'. 1NF atomic.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description for analytics and user understanding. For example, '10% off all orders over $50'.

plainFields.name: start_at
plainFields.description: When promotion is scheduled to begin. 3NF, atomic.

plainFields.name: end_at
plainFields.description: When promotion is scheduled to end. 3NF, atomic.

plainFields.name: active
plainFields.description: If this promotion is currently active. Support for dynamic toggling. 1NF atomic.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Created timestamp for audit trail. 1NF atomic.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp for history trace. 1NF atomic.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete for compliance. 3NF atomic, null if not deleted.

models.name: ai_mall_coupons
models.description: Coupons - Implements business requirements for code-based campaign offers as per promotions and loyalty system documentation. Supports stackable/exclusive coupon logic with enforced normalization. Example: 'WELCOME10' code for first order discount. Coupons can be linked to promotions and issued individually through coupon issuances. This model maintains referential integrity with ai_mall_promotions where 'promotion_id' is set, holding no calculated fields. 3NF compliance.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each coupon.

foreignFields.name: promotion_id
foreignFields.description: Associated promotion's ai_mall_promotions.id. Links the coupon to a high-level marketing event. May be null for one-off coupons. Referential integrity to ai_mall_promotions.

plainFields.name: code
plainFields.description: Unique coupon code for redemption (e.g., 'SUMMER2025'). 1NF atomic.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Description of coupon offer logic. Used for customer-facing messaging and analytics.

plainFields.name: type
plainFields.description: Coupon type, e.g. percentage/fixed/free_shipping. Used for validation logic. 1NF atomic.

plainFields.name: value
plainFields.description: Discount value for the coupon, as per type. 1NF atomic.

plainFields.name: min_purchase_amount
plainFields.description: Minimum spend required to activate this coupon. 3NF atomic (null if inapplicable).

plainFields.name: usage_limit
plainFields.description: Maximum number of global redemptions for coupon (anti-abuse control). 1NF atomic.

plainFields.name: per_user_limit
plainFields.description: Allowed usage count per user (anti-abuse control). 3NF atomic, null = unlimited.

plainFields.name: valid_from
plainFields.description: Coupon usable from this time (for scheduling window). 1NF atomic.

plainFields.name: valid_until
plainFields.description: Date/time coupon expires. 1NF atomic.

plainFields.name: stackable
plainFields.description: Whether this coupon can be combined with others. 1NF atomic.

plainFields.name: exclusive
plainFields.description: Whether coupon must be used alone (enforced exclusivity). 3NF atomic.

plainFields.name: enabled
plainFields.description: If this coupon is currently enabled in the system (admin toggling). 1NF atomic.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Created timestamp. 1NF atomic.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Updated timestamp. 1NF atomic.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete for audit/compliance. 3NF, null if not deleted.

models.name: ai_mall_coupon_issuances
models.description: Coupon Issuance Records - Represents every instance where a coupon is issued/granted to a particular user for redemption tracking, audit, and analytics. 3NF-compliant. Links to coupons and users, supporting anti-abuse and compliance tracks. Example: Record for single-user coupon issued to attract new customer.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each coupon issuance instance.

foreignFields.name: coupon_id
foreignFields.description: Coupon identifier (ai_mall_coupons.id). Links issuance to its coupon for validation and audit. Referential integrity enforced.

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: Issued-to user identifier (ai_mall_customers.id, external). Required for personalized coupon assignment. Referential integrity to external users table.

plainFields.name: issued_at
plainFields.description: When this coupon was issued. Used for redemption and audit trails. 1NF atomic.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Date/time this issued coupon expires (may differ from coupon's global expiry). 3NF atomic.

plainFields.name: redeemed
plainFields.description: Flag for usage status. True if user redeemed, else False. 1NF atomic.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation time (audit/compliance). 1NF atomic.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update time (audit/tracing). 1NF atomic.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp. 3NF atomic, null if not deleted.

models.name: ai_mall_coupon_usages
models.description: Coupon Usage Records - Each user redemption of a coupon, linked to the specific issuance and the corresponding order. 3NF compliance. Maintains full audit trace for compliance and fraud prevention. Example: User redeems a coupon on checkout, record is created for exact order-coupon relationship.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each coupon usage record.

foreignFields.name: issuance_id
foreignFields.description: Coupon issuance identifier (ai_mall_coupon_issuances.id) being redeemed. Referential integrity with issued coupon.

foreignFields.name: order_id
foreignFields.description: Order identifier (ai_mall_orders.id, external) for which coupon applied. Referential integrity to external orders table.

plainFields.name: used_at
plainFields.description: When the coupon was redeemed. 1NF atomic.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation time for audit. 1NF atomic.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Update time for audit/audit trail. 1NF atomic.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp for compliance/audit. 3NF, null if not deleted.

models.name: ai_mall_loyalty_tiers
models.description: Loyalty Tiers - Defines customer tier levels for the loyalty system (e.g., Silver, Gold, Platinum) as per business requirements. 3NF. No direct user-link; used in analytics and benefits assignment. Each row represents eligibility rules for a tier. Example: Gold = 10,000+ points. All keys/description fields are atomic and normalized.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key for each loyalty tier record.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Descriptive tier name (e.g., 'Platinum'). Must be unique. 1NF atomic.

plainFields.name: min_points
plainFields.description: Minimum point balance required to unlock this tier. 1NF atomic.

plainFields.name: max_points
plainFields.description: Upper bound for tier (null = unlimited). Used for automated tier upgrades. 3NF atomic.

plainFields.name: enabled
plainFields.description: Whether this tier is enabled by admin. 1NF atomic.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Created timestamp. 1NF atomic.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Updated timestamp. 1NF atomic.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete for audit/compliance. 3NF, null if not deleted.

models.name: ai_mall_loyalty_point_ledgers
models.description: Loyalty Point Ledgers - Tracks each instance of user loyalty point accrual/deduction for compliance, analytics, and accurate balance management. 3NF, atomic fields only. Each row is an atomic point movement, not a summary. Example: +200 for new order, -50 for redemption. Linked to user for exact balance trace. No aggregates stored.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key for each loyalty point ledger transaction.

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: User identifier for the points transaction (ai_mall_customers.id, external). Referential integrity to users domain.

plainFields.name: change_type
plainFields.description: Type: earn/redeem/adjust. String code for analytics and business logic. 1NF atomic.

plainFields.name: amount
plainFields.description: Point amount (earn=positive, redeem=negative, adjust=positive/negative). 3NF atomic.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Explanation for business logic, e.g., 'order_placement' or 'admin_correction'. 3NF atomic, optional.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Created timestamp for audit and ledgers. 1NF atomic.

models.name: ai_mall_deposits
models.description: Deposit Ledger - Manages store credits and similar compensation flows for regulatory and audit compliance; each record is a normalized, atomic adjustment. Linked to user for accurate, auditable ledgers. Example: Refund as deposit credit due to return. Tracks reason, value, user only; no non-normalized/cached fields present.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key for each deposit ledger transaction.

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: Customer account id for deposit/credit (ai_mall_customers.id, external). Referential integrity to users module.

plainFields.name: change_type
plainFields.description: Deposit transaction reason/type (e.g., issue, refund, adjustment, compensation). 1NF atomic.

plainFields.name: amount
plainFields.description: Amount of credit issued (can be negative if reversed). 3NF atomic.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Explanation string for audit trail (business logic free-text). 3NF atomic, optional.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Created timestamp for audit and compliance. 1NF atomic.

models.name: ai_mall_point_transactions
models.description:
Point Transaction Ledger - This implements the platform's requirement for a reliable, immutable audit trail of all point-related activities as outlined in the loyalty/promotion and auditing sections of the requirements (see 05_ai-mall_promotions-and-loyalty-systems.md and 09_ai-mall_security-compliance-accessibility.md).

Tracks every accrual, redemption, or adjustment of loyalty/mileage points for any user. Maintains 3NF normalization by modeling each transaction atomically (no aggregate fields, only point deltas per event). Example: when a customer earns points from an order, or redeems points at checkout, a row is created here. Supports full historical tracing for reversals, fraud investigation, and compliance/audit purposes.

Key relationships: references user (foreign key, e.g., ai_mall_customers.id), optionally associates to order or coupon, references rule for why points were changed. Special behavior: rows are immutable for audit; reversal is modeled as a new, opposite-amount transaction.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each point transaction.

foreignFields.name: ai_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged customer's {@link ai_mall_customers.id}. The user who owns this point transaction.

foreignFields.name: ai_mall_point_rule_id
foreignFields.description: Applied rule's {@link ai_mall_point_rules.id}. The business rule (e.g., reason or campaign) under which the points were created/consumed.

plainFields.name: change_type
plainFields.description: Type of transaction - Implements point event reason mapping. E.g., 'accrual' for earning, 'redemption' for spend, 'reversal', etc. Ensures normalization by storing atomic event type rather than embedding logic.

plainFields.name: amount
plainFields.description: Points added/subtracted. Always positive; sign (+/-) determines addition or subtraction. Enforces atomic point changes for each event.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional transaction detail for user-facing logs or admin/audit review. Maps to enhanced auditability requirement.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Transaction creation timestamp. Immutable, ensures strict order and unique event log. Used for audit, chronological tracing, balance calculation.

models.name: ai_mall_point_rules
models.description:
Point Rule Definitions - Implements the need for flexible, traceable point accrual/redemption business logic (see 05_ai-mall_promotions-and-loyalty-systems.md).

Stores the definition and configuration of all point-related rules and campaigns (e.g., 'Earn 2 points per $1 at category X', 'Birthday bonus', 'Refund adjustment'). Maintains normalization by separating rule logic from transaction and balance. Example: each time a point action occurs, it references a rule row here (either a standard accrual, event promo, or manual adjustment).

Key relationships: referenced by point transactions. Special behaviors: rules can be activated/deactivated, may include metadata/config for automation, can be time-bounded (start/end).

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each point rule.

plainFields.name: rule_code
plainFields.description: Unique code for rule. Implements requirement for auditable, human/machine readable business identifiers (e.g., 'JOIN_BONUS2025'). 3NF: allows easy rule lookup without denormalization.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Display name for the rule. Maps to business compliance and admin UI/analytics display requirements.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed explanation of the rule/logic (for admin/audit/UIs).

plainFields.name: active
plainFields.description: Is the rule currently in effect? Implements enable/disable flows for promotions and regulatory compliance. 3NF: no redundancy; just binary flag.

plainFields.name: start_at
plainFields.description: Rule effect start time. Allows time-based, scheduled point actions/promos. Nullable if always active.

plainFields.name: end_at
plainFields.description: Rule effect end time. Nullable if open-ended or permanent rule.

plainFields.name: metadata
plainFields.description: Optional JSON metadata for extensibility (e.g., custom rule configs, dynamic parameters).

models.name: ai_mall_point_balances
models.description:
Point Balances by User - Implements the requirement for instant user dashboard display of current point status (see promotions/loyalty UX guidelines). Serves as the current 'materialized' view of all point transactions, but fully normalized (not a denormalized/cached sum—actual materialized views would use 'mv_' prefix and only for reporting/performance).

Stores a user's current available (spendable) and pending (e.g., under review or lock-up) point balances. All balance changes derive exclusively from transactions (no manual updates permitted). Example: when a user earns or spends points, after successful transaction insert, this table is atomically updated. Key for customer UX, checkout validation, loyalty dashboards.

Key relationships: references ai_mall_customers (user), but does not duplicate history. Special behaviors: 1:1 with user; business rules prohibit negative available balances.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each user's balance row.

foreignFields.name: ai_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged customer's {@link ai_mall_customers.id}. One row per customer (1:1 constraint).

plainFields.name: available_points
plainFields.description: Current available (spendable) point balance. 0 or positive integer, always derived from transaction history. No redundancy—enforces normalization.

plainFields.name: pending_points
plainFields.description: Points pending (e.g., earned but not cleared, or locked). 0 or positive integer, never negative. Separation enables precise deduction flows, as required for order and refund handling. No aggregation/pre-calculation in this table; always normalized.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp for balance record. For concurrency control and user/account dashboard accuracy logging. Only updated on legitimate balance change event.

models.name: ai_mall_inquiries
models.description: [Inquiry] Implements inquiry registration in the Interaction & Personalization requirements. Allows customers to submit questions regarding products or orders, visible to sellers and optionally admins. Maintains 3NF via FKs to customer/product/order. Example: Customer asks if a product ships internationally, seller/admin responds via comments. Key relationships: ai_mall_customers, ai_mall_products, ai_mall_orders; commented via ai_mall_inquiry_comments.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged customer's {@link ai_mall_customers.id}. Authorship trace and follow-up.

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description: Related product's {@link ai_mall_products.id}. Enables catalog linkage and context.

foreignFields.name: order_id
foreignFields.description: Order's {@link ai_mall_orders.id} if relevant to purchase. Enables context escalation for support.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Inquiry summary/title. Requirements: concise topic for display/listing. Example: 'Shipping delay inquiry'.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Inquiry full content. Structurally distinct from comments. Example: 'When will this ship?'

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current process state (e.g., 'open','answered','closed','deleted'). Tracks and enables workflow filtering.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When the inquiry was created. Enables audit/chronology.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update. Enables audit, change tracking.

models.name: ai_mall_inquiry_comments
models.description: [Inquiry Comment] Implements communication/follow-up on inquiries per requirements (threaded support, role separation). Maintains 3NF, separate from ai_mall_inquiries. Supports moderation, threading via parent_id (self-reference), and role-based authorship.

foreignFields.name: inquiry_id
foreignFields.description: Parent inquiry's {@link ai_mall_inquiries.id}. Required FK for all comments.

foreignFields.name: author_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Author customer, if from customer role. Optional for multi-role system.

foreignFields.name: author_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Author seller, if from seller role.

foreignFields.name: author_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Author admin, if from admin role.

foreignFields.name: parent_id
foreignFields.description: Parent comment's {@link ai_mall_inquiry_comments.id}, supporting threaded replies.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Comment content. Implements threaded support content or follow-up.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Moderation/workflow state. (e.g., 'active','hidden','deleted')

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Update timestamp for audit trail.

models.name: ai_mall_reviews
models.description: [Product Review] Implements customer review/feedback on purchased products, fulfilling requirements of the Review system. 3NF maintained by referencing customer, product, and order by FK and separating review comments. Example: Customer leaves review after purchase, seller or admin responds via ai_mall_review_comments.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: Reviewer's {@link ai_mall_customers.id} (author FK for audit).

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description: Reviewed product's {@link ai_mall_products.id}.

foreignFields.name: order_id
foreignFields.description: Order context for verified review, nullable for edge/unfulfilled cases.

plainFields.name: rating_quality
plainFields.description: Quality aspect (1-5). Required for analytics and dashboard scoring.

plainFields.name: rating_value
plainFields.description: Value for money aspect (1-5).

plainFields.name: rating_delivery
plainFields.description: Delivery experience aspect (1-5).

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Review main text content. Not duplicated in comment table.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Review moderation/fraud state (e.g., 'active','hidden','deleted','flagged').

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Time review submitted.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last review update.

models.name: ai_mall_review_comments
models.description: [Review Comment] Implements comment thread for review system (feedback, moderation, replies). Maintains linkage to review, role-based authorship, self-referencing for threading.

foreignFields.name: review_id
foreignFields.description: FK to reviewed post {@link ai_mall_reviews.id}.

foreignFields.name: author_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Comment author if customer, optional.

foreignFields.name: author_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Comment author if seller, optional.

foreignFields.name: author_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Comment author if admin, optional.

foreignFields.name: parent_id
foreignFields.description: Self-reference for reply threading ({@link ai_mall_review_comments.id}).

plainFields.name: body

models.name: ai_mall_favorites
models.description:
Favorites Registry - This implements the requirement for customers to favorite products and easily access them for repeat viewing or purchase (from the Interaction & Personalization requirements in 06_ai-mall_interaction-and-personalization.md). 

Allows customers to quickly re-access items of interest, improving engagement and return visits. Ensures strict 3NF normalization, with each favorite stored atomically and referenced by user and product. For example, when a user 'favorites' a product, a record is created with references to both.

Key relationships: references customers (ai_mall_customers) and products (ai_mall_products).
Special behaviors: Enforces uniqueness (no duplicate favorites per user per product), supports soft deletion/audit trail by timestamps.

foreignFields.name: ai_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged customer's {@link ai_mall_customers.id}

foreignFields.name: ai_mall_product_id
foreignFields.description: Favorited product's {@link ai_mall_products.id}

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this favorite was created - Implements audit requirement for traceability and user engagement features. Used for sorting/display.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft-deletion timestamp - if set, marks this record as deleted without physical removal, for audit/compliance.

models.name: ai_mall_wishlists
models.description:
Wish List Registry - Implements the requirement for customers to create personal wish lists or buckets and organize/favorite products accordingly (per 06_ai-mall_interaction-and-personalization.md).

Allows users to group products for future purchase, gift lists, or themed collections. Maintains normalization by mapping each wish list to its user, with metadata fields. Used when a user creates a new wish list (e.g., "Birthday Gifts").

Key relationships: references customer table.
Special behaviors: Enforces 3NF. Includes metadata for name and visibility.

foreignFields.name: ai_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Owning customer's {@link ai_mall_customers.id}

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Wish list name/title - Implements user organizational requirement. For example, 'Summer Shoes', 'Birthday Gifts'.

plainFields.name: is_public
plainFields.description: Whether this wish list is visible to others - privacy/collections requirement.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when wish list was created - for sort/filter and audit.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of last modification - for edit tracking/audit.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft-deletion timestamp - for compliance and rollback/audit.

models.name: ai_mall_wishlist_items
models.description:
Wish List Item Linking Table - Implements the linking of products to explicit wish lists (per 06_ai-mall_interaction-and-personalization.md).

Each row represents a single product saved to a user's wish list. Maintains normalization (3NF) by linking wish list and product atomically, with unique constraint. Used to display all items in a user's wish list by joining on wish list ID.

Key relationships: references ai_mall_wishlists and ai_mall_products tables.
Special behaviors: Enforces uniqueness (no duplicate product per wish list).

foreignFields.name: ai_mall_wishlist_id

models.name: ai_mall_collections

Custom Collection Registry - Implements user scenario for creating custom groupings of products, including privacy and sharing features (see 06_ai-mall_interaction-and-personalization.md).

Allows customers to create thematic or public/private product groupings with displayable metadata. Maintains normalization by storing atomic metadata and customer reference only. Used when users curate a public collection for event sharing.

Key relationships: references ai_mall_customers.
Special behaviors: Includes privacy/public flag and soft deletion for compliance.

foreignFields.name: ai_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Founder/owner customer's {@link ai_mall_customers.id}

plainFields.name: label

Collection Item Linking Table - Implements connection of products to collections by users for custom group displays (per 06_ai-mall_interaction-and-personalization.md).

Enforces normalization by linking a collection to single products. Used to enumerate all products in a collection by joining to this table. Used when rendering a user's collection.

Key relationships: references ai_mall_collections and ai_mall_products.
Special behaviors: Unique constraint prevents duplicates, supports soft deletion and timestamp audit.

foreignFields.name: ai_mall_collection_id
foreignFields.description: Collection's {@link ai_mall_collections.id}

models.name: ai_mall_articles
models.description: Article entity - This implements the platform article/post requirement for news, blog content, or editorial material. Articles serve as informational or promotional content authored by admins (or sellers, if permitted). Each article can have multiple comments and be assigned to one or more article categories. Fully normalized by separating main article data, comments, and category mappings. For example, an admin can publish new feature updates, or a seller can post promotional articles. Key relationships: references to authors (admin or seller), links to category and comments. Special behaviors: articles can be edited or unpublished but retain audit trail via snapshots if needed.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each article.

foreignFields.name: author_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to admin author's {@link ai_mall_admins.id}. Indicates article is authored by an admin. Nullable if authored by seller.

foreignFields.name: author_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to seller author's {@link ai_mall_sellers.id}. Indicates article is authored by a seller. Nullable if authored by admin.

foreignFields.name: category_id
foreignFields.description: Assigned article category's {@link ai_mall_article_categories.id}. Categorizes article for navigation, filtering, or display/grouping.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Title of the article - Implements the requirement for article headline. Main descriptor for search, display, and navigation. Fully atomic and required.

plainFields.name: slug
plainFields.description: SEO-friendly slug/URL segment for the article. Used for human-readable and indexable links. Example: 'ai-mall-launch-event'. Ensures normalization by separating from title/body.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Main content body - Implements article textual/HTML content as fully normalized field. No derived or summary fields included. For example, product launch details, guides, etc.

plainFields.name: published
plainFields.description: Publication flag - Indicates whether article is publicly visible or in draft/unpublished state. Implements content moderation flow. Not calculated; atomic status only.

plainFields.name: pinned
plainFields.description: Pinned flag for featured or promoted articles. Atomic flag (true if highlighted), maintains fully normalized structure.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation timestamp for the article. Atomic event time, not derived. Enforces audit trail requirements.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp for the article. Used for audit and change tracking per non-functional requirements. Not calculated.

models.name: ai_mall_article_comments
models.description: Article comment entity - Implements the ability for users to comment on articles as per interaction and personalization requirements. Allows multiple comments per article, supports threaded/hierarchical replies via parent_id. Maintains 3NF by separating comment text, article association, and user identity. Usage example: customers, sellers, or admins can add discussion/comments on news, guides, etc. Key relationships: links to article, parent (for threads), and comment author (customer, seller, or admin). Special behaviors: moderation, visibility, and deletion handled at application layer.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each comment.

foreignFields.name: article_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to parent article's {@link ai_mall_articles.id}. Each comment belongs to one article.

foreignFields.name: author_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to commenting customer's {@link ai_mall_customers.id}, if comment was left by a customer. Nullable if comment by seller/admin.

foreignFields.name: author_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to commenting seller's {@link ai_mall_sellers.id}, if comment was left by a seller. Nullable if comment by customer/admin.

foreignFields.name: author_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to commenting admin's {@link ai_mall_admins.id}, if comment was left by an admin. Nullable if comment by customer/seller.

foreignFields.name: parent_id
foreignFields.description: Optional self-reference to parent comment ({@link ai_mall_article_comments.id}) for threaded discussions. Null for top-level comments, set for replies.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Main comment text body - Implements atomic requirement to store actual user comment content. Fully normalized; no derived sentiment or summary fields. For example: customer leaves question, seller provides answer.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation timestamp - Meets audit/auditability requirement for comment event. Not calculated.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last edit timestamp for the comment. Supports moderation and edit trail functionality per requirements.

models.name: ai_mall_article_categories
models.description: Article category entity - Implements requirement for grouping articles for organization, navigation, filtering, and SEO. Maintains 3NF by separating categorical metadata from articles. For example, guides, news, policy updates, etc. Each category can be assigned to multiple articles. Hierarchy (parent-child) allows nesting categories. Special behaviors: if parent_id is set, forms category tree; else is a root-level category. Application can enforce business logic on parent/child constraints.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each article category.

foreignFields.name: parent_id
foreignFields.description: Optional parent category's {@link ai_mall_article_categories.id} for category hierarchy and nesting. Null for root categories.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Category name - Implements the requirement for unique, human-readable article category label. Ensures normalization.

plainFields.name: slug
plainFields.description: SEO-friendly category slug for URLs/navigation. Must be unique within categories. Example: 'news-updates'. Maintains normalization by not duplicating category name.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional category description - Implements meta/SEO or UI tooltip requirement. Nullable, not required.

models.name: ai_mall_analytics_events
models.description:
Analytics Event Entity - This implements the requirements for tracking distinct analytics events as demanded in the advanced analytics and AI documentation. 

Business explanation: Each row represents a single captured analytics event (click, page view, purchase, search, error) generated by any user or system process. Maintains 3NF compliance—event details and context are atomic and not derived. For example, when a customer adds an item to their cart, a new analytics event is created referencing its type and holding contextual payload (serialized JSON). 

Key relationships: Ties to ai_mall_analytics_event_types for type definition, can reference actor tables (not directly modeled here). 
Special behaviors: Loosely coupled with user/session IDs for flexibility; all business logic for attribution is handled externally.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each analytics event record.

foreignFields.name: event_type_id
foreignFields.description: Event type reference - Links to event type definition in {@link ai_mall_analytics_event_types.id} to ensure event categorization adheres to system-defined taxonomy. Relationship is required for classification.

plainFields.name: occurred_at
plainFields.description: Event Occurrence Timestamp - Implements the requirement to record the exact UTC time of the event occurrence. Maintains strict normalization with explicit, unambiguous timestamps. For example, used for all time-based analytics, daily active users, or sequence analysis.

plainFields.name: actor_id
plainFields.description: Actor Reference (Loose/Flexible) - Optionally associates an event with any system actor (customer, seller, admin). Implements the requirement for user attribution analytics (inferred by external joins). Maintains normalization by not duplicating user state; can be null for system/bot events.

plainFields.name: session_id
plainFields.description: Session Reference (Loose/Flexible) - Optionally attributes the event to a browsing session or device identity for anonymous event tracking. Enforces normalization by keeping only the session UUID here; session metadata is external.

plainFields.name: context_payload
plainFields.description: Contextual Event Data (JSON/String) - Stores serialized event context payload (click details, product IDs, metadata) as a JSON string field for semi-structured extensibility. Ensures normalization by never repeating structured relations; payload structure is externally enforced. Example: '{"productId": "abc-123", "action": "add_to_cart", "value": 8990 }'.

plainFields.name: ip_address
plainFields.description: IP Address - Implements the requirement to optionally log origin IP for risk or source analysis. Ensures atomicity by storing only address string. Usage: geo-analytics, fraud investigations, etc.

models.name: ai_mall_analytics_event_types
models.description:
Analytics Event Type Entity - Implements cataloging all event types (category, action codes) as defined in the advanced analytics system requirements. 

Business purpose: Each entry defines a logical type of analytics event such as 'page_view', 'add_to_cart', 'purchase', 'error', etc. Maintains 3NF by separating event occurrence from event taxonomy. For example, when a new event type such as 'wishlist_add' is required, it's created here and referenced by all relevant event records. 

Key relationships: Referenced by events; not directly tied to user/session. 
Special behaviors: Type codes and human-readable names must be unique; descriptions provide API and analytics clarity.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for event type definition.

plainFields.name: code
plainFields.description: Event Type Code - Implements code-based requirement for system-wide event type consistency (e.g., 'page_view', 'add_to_cart'). Must be unique. Maintains normalization by de-coupling event occurrence from type metadata. Example: Used in analytics queries for grouping.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Event Type Name - Implements requirement for human-readable descriptive name for event type. Example: 'Page View', 'Cart Add'. Supports admin-facing analytics UI lookup.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Event Type Description - Implements requirement for extended explanation, API tooltip, or audit notes. Maintains normalization by attaching only to type, not to each event.

models.name: ai_mall_user_dashboards
models.description:
User Dashboard Configuration Entity - Implements requirement to let each user (actor) configure personal analytics dashboards as described in analytics and personalization documentation. 

Business purpose: Each record stores dashboard configuration for a specific user—what widgets or reports are pinned, layout configuration as JSON, and timestamps. Maintains 3NF with atomic user association and configuration payload. Used to persist user dashboard state across sessions and devices.

Key relationships: References actor ID (can be customer, seller, or admin - stored as UUID; resolving the actual actor is external).
Special behaviors: One dashboard config per actor (enforced by unique index); supports time-based filtering and historical layout snapshots.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each dashboard configuration.

foreignFields.name: actor_id
foreignFields.description: Actor/User Reference - Attributed to a user (any actor type) via system UUID. Ensures every dashboard belongs to exactly one user; resolving actual user is handled in application logic. Not nullable.

plainFields.name: dashboard_payload
plainFields.description: Dashboard Configuration Payload - Implements storage of widget/report configuration as serialized JSON. Maintains strict normalization as atomic config blob only; no duplicated data. Example: '{"widgets": ["sales_chart", "visits_map"]}'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Dashboard Created Timestamp - Date/time of configuration creation. Ensures atomic record for audit trail. Used for query, filtering, and sorting.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Dashboard Updated Timestamp - Last modification time of dashboard. Ensures traceability of configuration changes and auditability.

models.name: ai_mall_campaign_metrics
models.description:
Campaign Analytics Metrics Entity - Implements requirements for campaign/promotion performance measurement as required by the promotions and analytics documentation. 

Business purpose: Each row aggregates or stores campaign metrics (impressions, clicks, redemption counts, revenue, cost, ROI) for a specific campaign and date/time bucket. 
Maintains 3NF—metrics are always external/per campaign/per period, never pre-calculated totals. Used by seller/admin dashboards and reporting tools.

Key relationships: References campaign or promotion via UUID (campaign table external to this domain, relationship by UUID only).
Special behaviors: Metric records are independent and domain-normalized—never cache/copy derived aggregates. Composite uniqueness enforced by (campaign_id, period_start).

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for campaign metric row.

foreignFields.name: campaign_id
foreignFields.description: Marketing Campaign/Promotion Reference - Associates metric row to a logical campaign/promotion/offer (defined externally). UUID only; campaign metadata resolved externally. Not nullable.

plainFields.name: period_start
plainFields.description: Metrics Period Start - Implements reporting granularity (e.g., daily, hourly) for time series analytics. Enforces normalization with explicit period-bucketed data only. Used in charts and time-based queries.

plainFields.name: impressions
plainFields.description: Impressions Count - Implements raw metric requirement for number of times campaign was displayed. Atomic count (not accumulated). Maintains normalization as primitive numeric fact only.

plainFields.name: clicks
plainFields.description: Clicks Count - Implements requirement to store number of user clicks on the campaign. Atomic, fully normalized field, not a calculation.

plainFields.name: redemptions
plainFields.description: Redemptions Count - Requirement to track coupon/promotion redemption count. Maintains atomic normalization.

plainFields.name: revenue
plainFields.description: Revenue Attributed - Requirement for revenue measurement attributed to campaign. Maintains strict normalization as atomic recorded value (never a calculation or cache).

plainFields.name: cost
plainFields.description: Cost Attributed - Requirement for cost metric (discounts, spend) attributed to campaign. Stored as atomic numeric value (never as a calculated or derived field).

plainFields.name: roi
plainFields.description: ROI - Implements requirement to persist measured return on investment for the specific campaign/time. Must be atomic and calculated externally; never duplicated/derived in reporting queries.

### `ai_mall_channels`

Platform sales channel configuration - This implements the cross-channel and modular marketplace requirement from 'Architecture & Extensibility (07_ai-mall_architecture-and-extensibility.md)'. Provides foundational separation for mall operations by defining unique sales channels (web, app, third-party). Maintains 3NF structure by keeping channel-specific configuration here, without duplicating in lower-level business tables. Example: creation of a 'BrandA Global Web Store' or 'Mobile App Korea'. Key relationships: Referenced by sections, categories, file usages. Special behaviors: Channel can be disabled without deletion for staged launches or regulatory holds.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `code`: Unique identifier for the sales channel. Implements channel abstraction reference. Allows for lookup and management by business and system APIs. Example: 'KR_WEB', 'US_MOBILE'. Must be unique.
- `name`: Human-readable channel label. Example: 'Korea Web Store', 'Global Mobile App'.
- `brand`: Brand association for multi-brand platforms. Example: 'BrandA', 'GenericMall'.
- `enabled`: Whether this channel is currently active/published to users.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the channel was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp for the last channel update.

### `ai_mall_sections`

Channel sections configuration - Implements extensible, configurable sections for each sales channel, as described in 'Architecture & Extensibility'. Business purpose: Allows flexible segmentation within a channel (e.g., Electronics, Lifestyle, Flash Sale). Maintains 3NF by holding only section-level config/reference—products/content are managed separately. Example: a channel may have 'Home', 'Deals', or 'Electronics' sections. Key relationships: Links to [ai_mall_channels.id](#ai_mall_channels).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `ai_mall_channel_id`: Parent channel's [ai_mall_channels.id](#ai_mall_channels). Each section is tied to a channel, enforcing modular configuration. Required foreign key association.
- `code`: Unique identifier for section within the channel.
- `name`: User-facing section name (e.g., 'Flash Sale', 'Kids').
- `order`: Sort order of sections within a channel.
- `enabled`: Is this section active and visible on the channel?
- `created_at`: Timestamp section was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp for the last section update.

### `ai_mall_categories`

Flexible multi-level taxonomy for mall navigation - Implements hierarchical category management from 'Product & Content Management'. Enables unlimited nesting/category grouping for products and content. Maintains strict normalization by keeping category structure atomic and storing only hierarchy metadata here (not product links). Example: creation of 'Electronics > Phones > Smartphones', reordering, reparenting. Key relationships: Optional parent-child self-reference allows tree structure.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `parent_id`: Parent category's [ai_mall_categories.id](#ai_mall_categories). Enables recursive taxonomy. Nullable root-level. Maintains hierarchical structure in 3NF.
- `code`: Unique business identifier for the category. Example: 'ELEC_SMARTPHONES', 'TOYS_OUTDOOR'.
- `name`: Display name for category (multi-lingual UI supported at app layer).
- `level`: Category nesting depth (e.g., 0=root, 1=child, 2=grandchild).
- `order`: Sort order within siblings.
- `enabled`: Is the category active and visible for filtering/browsing?
- `created_at`: Timestamp category was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp for the last update.

### `ai_mall_files`

Attachment and file repository for mall resources - Implements file/media management as in 'Architecture (07_ai-mall_architecture-and-extensibility.md)'. Manages all uploaded files (images, videos, docs), storing metadata but not raw content. Example: product images, manuals, admin banners. Used by products, promotions, articles, etc. Business logic for file lifecycle (expiry, visibility) starts here.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `uri`: Permanent location of the file in cloud, CDN, or on-prem storage.
- `name`: Original file name with extension.
- `type`: Media type (MIME), e.g., 'image/png'.
- `size`: File size in bytes.
- `created_at`: Upload timestamp for audit and security reviews.
- `expires_at`: Optional expiration/deletion timestamp.

### `ai_mall_file_usages`

Mapping of files to business resources (products, channels, etc.) - Implements domain-agnostic usage log as described in 'Architecture'. Enables the same file to be attached to many business entities across domains, while separate from core file repository. Maintains 3NF: no reference info is stored in ai_mall_files; all usage links and field-specific meta go here. Example: link file id X to 'cover_image' of product Y. Special behaviors: file usage field enables typed attachments.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `ai_mall_file_id`: Referenced file's [ai_mall_files.id](#ai_mall_files). Required foreign key association.
- `usage_domain`: Domain of usage, e.g., 'product', 'promotion', 'article'.
- `usage_field`: Specific field context (e.g., 'cover_image').
- `entity_id`: UUID of the linked business entity (product, channel, section, etc.).
- `created_at`: Timestamp usage link was established.

### `ai_mall_api_gateways`

API Gateway registry/coordination - Implements security, endpoint, and routing control as described in 'Architecture'. Records metadata for each API gateway (core, internal, partner, test environments). Maintains 3NF: endpoint/routing data only, logs/stats are segregated elsewhere. Example: 'Public Core Gateway', 'Partner Channel Gateway'. Special behaviors: Gateways can be enabled/disabled for maintenance.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `code`: Unique gateway code. Example: 'CORE', 'PARTNER', 'TESTNET'.
- `name`: Display name/label for management UI.
- `base_url`: Base endpoint URL (e.g., 'https://api.mall.com/core').
- `enabled`: Whether this gateway is currently handling traffic.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when gateway was added.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp for the last gateway update.

### `ai_mall_audit_logs`

System-wide audit trail for compliance and troubleshooting - Implements audit log requirements from 'Security, Compliance & Accessibility'. Captures every critical action (user, admin, system) in a unified, immutable ledger for security and compliance. Maintains 3NF; audit log is append-only, no business data is duplicated. Example: admin disables a channel, user edits their role. Links actions to actor/entity via actor_id, entity_domain, and entity_id. All cross-table references are soft for extensibility.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `action`: Canonical name of action performed (e.g., 'channel_disable').
- `actor_role`: Role performing the action (e.g., 'admin', 'seller', 'system').
- `actor_id`: UUID of user/system performing the action.
- `entity_domain`: Entity domain this log references (e.g., 'channel').
- `entity_id`: UUID of the entity record acted upon.
- `ip`: IP address linked to the action.
- `details`: Structured or free-form log payload with action metadata/data.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the action/log was recorded.

### `ai_mall_settings`

Global and module-specific configuration registry - Implements platform-wide and modular configuration patterns from 'Architecture'. Stores key-value config for all mall subsystems (feature flags, UI settings, 3rd-party integration keys). Every setting is a separate row with unique key, value, and optional group/domain. Example: toggling AI segments, maintenance windows. Fully normalized.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `key`: Canonical config key (e.g., 'feature/recommendations.enabled').
- `value`: Current value for the key (string-encoded for flexibility).
- `group`: Configuration domain/group (e.g., 'feature').
- `description`: Optional description for admin UI, change log, or documentation.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the key was created.
- `updated_at`: Last modified time for this key/value.

### `ai_mall_customers`

Customer accounts - This implements the platform's customer account system from the user role and management requirements. Business users marked as customers for ownership of carts, orders, reviews, and personalization. Maintains 3NF by using normalized foreign keys to auth/user states. For example, a customer making a purchase will be linked here. Key relationships: references user profile, authentication, active state. Special behaviors: only non-admin, non-seller users belong here; customers can transition to seller.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `user_profile_id`: Belonged profile's [ai_mall_user_profiles.id](#ai_mall_user_profiles). Profile association for customer details and preference data. Required for linking demographic and personalization info.
- `authentication_id`: Authentication details [ai_mall_authentications.id](#ai_mall_authentications). Secures login credentials. Required for SSO, OAuth, multi-factor.
- `user_state_id`: Current state [ai_mall_user_states.id](#ai_mall_user_states). Shows if active, suspended, pending. Used for soft deletion and compliance audit.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of account creation. Implements onboarding flow compliance.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of last update. Auditing user changes.

### `ai_mall_sellers`

Seller accounts - Implements the merchant/seller role from requirements. Seller ownership over storefronts, product listings, and order fulfillment. Maintains 3NF; separated from customer/admin for permissioning. For example, a merchant dashboard references this. Key relationships: links to user profile and authentication. Special behaviors: future role upgrade/downgrade mapping.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `user_profile_id`: Belonged profile's [ai_mall_user_profiles.id](#ai_mall_user_profiles). Tied to individual or business profile for seller.
- `authentication_id`: Authentication source [ai_mall_authentications.id](#ai_mall_authentications). Seller login.
- `user_state_id`: Account status [ai_mall_user_states.id](#ai_mall_user_states). Active/verified/suspended checks.
- `created_at`: Seller account creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Seller record last update.

### `ai_mall_admins`

Admin operator accounts - Implements the admin role from user roles requirements. Used for full access, compliance monitoring, and global configuration. Maintains full normalization and strict isolation from customer/seller models. Example usage: admin dashboards and audit logs reference this entity. Key relationships: profile, authentication, state. Special behavior: audit logging and permission elevation/revocation.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `user_profile_id`: Admin profile reference [ai_mall_user_profiles.id](#ai_mall_user_profiles). Admin identity; critical for operations.
- `authentication_id`: Authentication details [ai_mall_authentications.id](#ai_mall_authentications). Responsible for login traceability and MFA.
- `user_state_id`: Current admin state [ai_mall_user_states.id](#ai_mall_user_states). For privilege control & suspension.
- `created_at`: Admin record creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp for last admin record update.

### `ai_mall_user_profiles`

User profile master record - Implements unified identity and profile normalization from requirements. Profiles can be reused/linked across roles (customer/seller/admin). Maintains 3NF and prevents duplicate user records per person/email. For example, profile settings update or role transition occurs here. Key relationships: links to all role tables, not just one. Special behaviors: versioned changes, personal detail enrichment.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `email`: Primary email address. Implements contact identity. Uniqueness across users. Used for login, notification, and compliance.
- `phone_number`: Optional phone for user. Used in authentication and notification flows.
- `full_name`: Full name per user profile. Used in personalization and communications.
- `nickname`: User's chosen nickname. Shown publicly in reviews, inquiries, etc.
- `avatar_url`: Avatar/profile photo URL for UI. Maintains normalization. Used in user settings screen, not business logic.
- `created_at`: Profile creation timestamp. Audit/compliance.
- `updated_at`: Profile updated timestamp. Tracing edits/auditing.

### `ai_mall_authentications`

User authentication credentials and methods - Implements credential and authentication records from requirement. Aggregates authentication factors (password hash, SSO/OAuth, MFA tokens) while linking to profiles. Maintains normalization, supports flexible auth provider integration. For example, signing in checks this entity. Key relationships: referenced by customer/seller/admin; ties to user profile. Special behaviors: securely stores only hashes/tokens, never plaintext secrets.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `user_profile_id`: Linked profile's [ai_mall_user_profiles.id](#ai_mall_user_profiles). Supports auditing/attribution of auth events.
- `auth_type`: Type of authentication (e.g., 'password','oauth','sso','sms'). Fulfills identity management flexibility.
- `identifier`: Principal ID (username, email, OAuth sub). Implements login state. Calculated at login. Needs to be unique for provider/user.
- `credential_hash`: Credential hash/token (never raw passwords). Ensures security compliance. Used for login validation only.
- `mfa_enabled`: Is Multi-Factor Auth enabled. Implements compliance, audit, and security hardening. Used for step-up auth flows.
- `created_at`: Credential record created at.
- `updated_at`: Credential record last updated at.

### `ai_mall_roles`

Role master - Implements business rule management for user roles (customer, seller, admin, and future custom roles). 3NF normalization, supports extensible platform role-based permissions. For example, role assignment/upgrade occurs here. Key relationships: role_assignments, used by core tables. Special behaviors: reserved roles enforced for compliance (cannot delete base roles).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `code`: Unique role code (e.g., 'customer', 'seller', 'admin'). Implements enum-like role logic throughout platform. Used for user gating, permission checks.
- `name`: Translatable display name. E.g., 'Customer', 'Seller', 'Admin'. Used in UIs.
- `description`: Long-form explanation/description of the role. For admin UIs and auditing. E.g., rationale for this role's permissions.
- `created_at`: Role record created at.
- `updated_at`: Role record last updated at.

### `ai_mall_role_assignments`

User-role assignment mapping - Implements user-to-role assignment per requirements for flexible permissioning and transitions. Supports audit tracking of who/why/when a user received or lost a role. Maintains 3NF (separate entity for reassignments and audit trail). For example, transitioning a customer to a seller creates a new assignment. Key relationships: user (profile), role; each user can have multiple role assignments over time. Special behaviors: tracks assignment/detachment reason/timing for audit and rollback.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `user_profile_id`: User being assigned [ai_mall_user_profiles.id](#ai_mall_user_profiles). User for the assignment. Allows one-to-many mapping (user can have multiple roles over time).
- `role_id`: Assigned role [ai_mall_roles.id](#ai_mall_roles). Links assignment to the role entity.
- `assigned_at`: Timestamp of role assignment creation.
- `detached_at`: Timestamp of role detachment/deactivation (null if still active). Implements access revocation.
- `reason`: Human-readable description of the assignment/detachment reason (optional). Used for audit logging.

### `ai_mall_user_states`

User state system - Implements state management for active, suspended, pending verification, or deleted users. Centralizes state for all roles to ensure consistent permission and compliance handling. Maintains 3NF; no duplication of state indicator in user records. For example: when customer is suspended, this state is referenced. Key relationships: referenced by all actor tables. Special behaviors: state transitions are logged, only valid states exist here.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `code`: Unique code identifying the state (e.g., 'active', 'suspended', 'pending', 'deleted'). Used for fast gating and compliance audits.
- `name`: Translatable state name ('Active','Suspended','Pending','Deleted'). For admin UIs and user logs.
- `description`: Human/long-form description of state. For audit/compliance and admin reference. E.g., when/how state is assigned.
- `created_at`: Record state creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: State record last updated at.
