Product/variant images - Implements multi-image storage. Each image links to product or variant, normalized (no repeat data). Example: an image belongs to a main product or a specific variant. 3NF. Related: ai_mall_files for file storage.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `ai_mall_product_id`: Owned product's [ai_mall_products.id](#ai_mall_products). Parent product for this image. Nullable for variant-only images.
- `ai_mall_product_variant_id`: Owned variant's [ai_mall_product_variants.id](#ai_mall_product_variants). Images linked to a specific variant.
- `ai_mall_file_id`: Physical file's [ai_mall_files.id](#ai_mall_files).
- `alt_text`: Image alt-text for accessibility/SEO. Example: 'Red wireless earbuds'.
- `order_index`: Order in product gallery.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when image entry was created.

### `ai_mall_product_tags`

Product tags - Implements tagging per requirements for findability and recommendation tuning. Each row links one tag to a product. Example: 'Bluetooth'. 3NF; no tag list repetition.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `ai_mall_product_id`: Associated product's [ai_mall_products.id](#ai_mall_products).
- `tag`: Tag keyword/phrase. Example: 'wireless'.
- `created_at`: When tag was applied.

### `ai_mall_product_attributes`

Custom attributes per product - Implements flexible attribute system (e.g., material, battery). Strict 3NF: name-value per row; atomic. Example: 'Material: Aluminum'. Key: references product.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `ai_mall_product_id`: Target product's [ai_mall_products.id](#ai_mall_products).
- `attribute_name`: Name/key of attribute. Example: 'Material'. 3NF: atomic.
- `attribute_value`: Value for attribute. Example: 'Aluminum'.
- `created_at`: Attribute creation date.

### `ai_mall_inventories`

Inventory control - Atomically normalized per-location inventory tracking. Example: 'Variant A' at 'Warehouse 1' vs 'Warehouse 2'. Strict 3NF: per-location-per-variant, no aggregates. Related: variant.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `ai_mall_product_variant_id`: Product variant's [ai_mall_product_variants.id](#ai_mall_product_variants).
- `location_label`: Inventory location. Example: 'Main Warehouse'.
- `quantity`: Stock count. Example: 25.
- `updated_at`: Inventory change timestamp.

### `ai_mall_brands`

Product brands meta table - Used for normalized catalog structure (referenced by ai_mall_products). 3NF: one row per brand. Example: 'Sony'.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `name`: Brand display name. Example: 'Sony'.
- `logo_url`: URL for logo image.
- `description`: Brand introduction/description.
- `created_at`: Creation record.

### `ai_mall_category_products`

Junction table for product-category (M:N) - Each row links one product to one category (no arrays in product). Example: Product in 'Electronics' and 'Gadgets'.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `ai_mall_product_id`: Linked product's [ai_mall_products.id](#ai_mall_products).
- `ai_mall_category_id`: Linked category's [ai_mall_categories.id](#ai_mall_categories) (Systematic domain).
- `order_index`: Order or position in category for custom sort. Example: 1.

### `ai_mall_product_snapshots`

Snapshot table for product history - Versioning, audit, rollback of product record changes. Every change yields a snapshot here. For rollback/compliance/history. Example: each publish/edit/retract action creates a new row. 3NF: no denormalization.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `ai_mall_product_id`: Referenced product's [ai_mall_products.id](#ai_mall_products).
- `snapshot_json`: Serialized snapshot (JSON) of all product fields.
- `created_at`: When snapshot was written.

### `ai_mall_carts`

Shopping Cart entity - This implements the persistent multi-seller, cross-device cart requirement from the requirements document (see 04_ai-mall_cart-and-order-processing.md, 'Cart Management'). 

This model stores a customer's current shopping cart, supporting persistent and session-based cart recovery. Maintains 3NF compliance: only core atomic cart attributes are stored, with all related items separated into ai_mall_cart_items. For example, a user logs in from any device and retrieves a unique cart instance. 

Key relationships: One-to-many with [ai_mall_cart_items](#ai_mall_cart_items) (cart items), many-to-one with [ai_mall_customers](#ai_mall_customers) (cart owner, from Actors domain), and optional link to [ai_mall_cart_sessions](#ai_mall_cart_sessions) (enables device/session association). 
Special behaviors: Soft deletion via 'deleted_at', automatic restoration logic during login/session merge.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for the cart instance.
- `ai_mall_customer_id`: Belonged customer's [ai_mall_customers.id](#ai_mall_customers); identifies the cart owner. Implements cross-device and session merge logic.
- `ai_mall_cart_session_id`: Optional link to shopping session [ai_mall_cart_sessions.id](#ai_mall_cart_sessions). Used for session-persistent/guest carts before user login/merge. Nullable.
- `created_at`: Cart creation timestamp - Implements audit/logging requirement. Represents when the cart was first created by the user or system. 3NF compliance: atomic event date only.
- `updated_at`: Cart last modified timestamp - Required for supporting auto-sync and concurrency control (e.g., real-time cart merging). 3NF compliance: captures only last update event.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp for recoverable cart deletion. Implements audit-log and logical delete without physical removal. Null if active.

### `ai_mall_cart_items`

Shopping Cart Item entity - This implements persistent, multi-product-item cart tracking, enabling dynamic update/merge logic per 04_ai-mall_cart-and-order-processing.md ('Cart Management', 'Real-time validation of inventory, dynamic pricing, and discount eligibility').

Stores precise entries for each product/variant in a cart. Maintains strict 3NF by storing only atomic item attributes; product/variant details are referenced, never duplicated. For example, each line in the cart—product + variant + quantity + pricing context—is an entry here.

Key relationships: Many-to-one with [ai_mall_carts](#ai_mall_carts) (cart header), references [ai_mall_products](#ai_mall_products) and [ai_mall_product_variants](#ai_mall_product_variants) (from Products domain) for the selected product version, and links back to customers through the cart. 
Special behaviors: Supports atomic updates per item; does not cache pricing, stock, or totals (calculated at checkout/time-of-use).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for a cart line item.
- `ai_mall_cart_id`: Belonged cart's [ai_mall_carts.id](#ai_mall_carts). Ensures item grouping to a specific persistent or session cart.
- `ai_mall_product_id`: Product ([ai_mall_products.id](#ai_mall_products)) added to the cart—foreign key to Products domain. Only atomic product id is tracked; all product details are externalized for 3NF.
- `ai_mall_product_variant_id`: Product variant ([ai_mall_product_variants.id](#ai_mall_product_variants)) selected in cart. Implements fine-grained inventory and pricing per variant, never duplicated here (3NF).
- `quantity`: Quantity of selected product/variant in the cart. 3NF: atomic count only. For example, 2 means 'user wants two of this variant'. Must be positive integer, enforced at application layer.
- `added_at`: Timestamp when item was first added to cart. For concurrency control and audit logs. 3NF: atomic event time.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when item was last updated (e.g., quantity changed). Supports multi-session merge, audit trail. 3NF: atomic update time only.

### `ai_mall_cart_sessions`

Cart Session entity - Implements the guest/anonymous shopping session persistence per requirements (04_ai-mall_cart-and-order-processing.md: 'Cart Management', 'Session resilience').

Tracks session-specific shopping carts for users who have not signed in, supporting cart restoration on reconnect/crash recovery. Maintains 3NF: atomic cart-session mapping only; all business logic occurs at application layer.

Key relationships: May be linked by [ai_mall_carts](#ai_mall_carts), allowing a session cart to be merged into a user's cart on login (one-to-many or one-to-one depending on user flow).
Special behaviors: May be cleaned up on session expiry; soft-deleted via 'deleted_at'.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for the cart session.
- `session_key`: Unique browser/device/session identifier, typically a secure random string or UUID. Used for mapping anonymous carts, preserving session state across reconnects. 3NF: atomic value only.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when session was created. Used for session lifecycle and audit.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when this cart session was last used or modified. Enables cleanup and status tracking.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp. Null if session active. Implements safe lifecycle and recovery logic.

### `ai_mall_orders`

Order Entity - This implements the order tracking and management requirements from the requirements analysis (primarily from Cart & Order Processing and referenced in Promotions/Loyalty logic). 

This model records the core details of a transaction (customer, seller, order status, channel, timestamps). Maintains strict 3NF compliance: all item/product/fulfillment/payment detail is normalized into related tables. Example: a customer places an order spanning multiple sellers; each order instance is tracked here, referencing customer, channel, and initial status. 

Key relationships: Links to customer (Actors), seller (Actors), order status, channel (Systematic), and supports referencing payments and fulfillments. Special behaviors: immutable order_id, stateful via status referencing, all denormalized (summaries, counted totals) reside in separate materialized views only.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each order record.
- `ai_mall_customer_id`: Belonged customer's [ai_mall_customers.id](#ai_mall_customers) - customer placing the order.
- `ai_mall_seller_id`: Belonged seller's [ai_mall_sellers.id](#ai_mall_sellers) - seller fulfilling this order split (multi-seller support).
- `ai_mall_channel_id`: Related channel's [ai_mall_channels.id](#ai_mall_channels) - sales channel on which the order was placed.
- `ai_mall_order_status_id`: Current order status [ai_mall_order_statuses.id](#ai_mall_order_statuses) - points to order state (placed, paid, shipped, etc).
- `external_order_code`: External Order Code - Implements third-party channel or system code assignment, used for reconciliation with partners/logistic systems. Normalization is kept by not duplicating core IDs, only allowing system-of-record pointers here. Example: Shopify order code.
- `gift`: Gift Indicator - Implements requirement to track if order is a gift (special instructions on fulfillment/delivery). 3NF is maintained: related detail/notes handled via fulfillment or snapshot entities.
- `buy_request_memo`: Customer Order Memo - Implements capturing of purchase comment/request. Normalized: only memo, not aggregation or status flags. Example: 'Please deliver after 6pm'.
- `created_at`: Order creation timestamp. Implements requirement for auditability and time-based querying. 3NF is kept by not storing derivative or summary values.
- `updated_at`: Order updated/modification timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp for audit/history compliance. Null if active.

### `ai_mall_order_items`

Order Item Entity - Implements the requirement to record normalized line item details for each order, per item/SKU, covering the structure outlined in Cart & Order Processing functional requirements. Strictly 3NF: product info/entity reference only, no denormalized rollups or calculations.

Business purpose: Each record is a unique product (and variant) ordered, with quantity, price, and per-item status. Example: Order containing 2 products generates 2 records here. Key relationships: links to ai_mall_orders, ai_mall_product_variants (Products), ai_mall_order_statuses. Special behaviors: separate status per item for partial fulfillment, references all by foreign key.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each order item.
- `ai_mall_order_id`: Reference to parent order's [ai_mall_orders.id](#ai_mall_orders).
- `ai_mall_product_variant_id`: Product variant SKU's [ai_mall_product_variants.id](#ai_mall_product_variants).
- `ai_mall_order_status_id`: Status of this order item [ai_mall_order_statuses.id](#ai_mall_order_statuses). Enables split fulfillment or returns per item.
- `requested_quantity`: Quantity ordered - directly implements required per-SKU quantity tracking and normalization by separating item quantities to rows, not as aggregates. Example: 3 of SKU X, 2 of SKU Y across 2 rows.
- `confirmed_price`: Confirmed Price - Business meaning: price per item (including discounts) set at the time of order item confirmation. Complies with 3NF as all calculations reside in reporting/materialized views.
- `confirmed_currency`: Currency of confirmed_price (e.g., USD, KRW). 3NF: currency stored per item for multi-currency support without denormalization.
- `product_title_snapshot`: Product Title at Time of Order - Implements audit-traceable ordering (snapshot pattern). Normalized: Stores only the business-facing title as it existed at order time.

### `ai_mall_order_statuses`

Order Status Entity - Implements requirement for flexible, auditable order state tracking per order and per item. All business logic around order state transitions relies on these enumerations. Normalized: no aggregate or rollup data. Example: 'placed', 'paid', 'shipped', 'completed', 'cancelled', etc.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each order status.
- `code`: Status Code - Short machine-friendly identifier (e.g., placed, paid, shipped, cancelled) supporting business rules. Normalization: Used by foreign-key reference, not duplicated in other tables.
- `label`: Status Display Label (user-facing string) - Implements multi-language/locale friendly display. Normalized by keeping locale-specific data in separate translation/supporting tables.
- `description`: Long-form business description for the status - implements audit and UI display requirements.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp, supporting audit/log requirements.

### `ai_mall_order_snapshots`

Order Snapshot Entity - Implements full audit-traceable and temporal storage for version history (requirement: snapshot pattern for order editing/auditing). Each record represents an immutable version of an order at a point in time. 3NF: no rollups, denormalized reporting, or calculated values here; only atomic snapshots at the time of update or significant event.

Business purpose: Enables rollback and change tracking. Example: changing shipping address triggers creation of a new snapshot. Links to parent order and stores who/what/when for inspections/audits.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each order snapshot.
- `ai_mall_order_id`: Parent order's [ai_mall_orders.id](#ai_mall_orders) - reference to the order whose state is snapshot.
- `ai_mall_admin_id`: Reference admin actor's [ai_mall_admins.id](#ai_mall_admins) - identifies who/what made the order edit or override.
- `snapshot_json`: Immutable JSON snapshot of the order state and details at this point in time. Normalization is maintained by not storing reporting/derived information, only the original state. Example: Change in fulfillment state, item list, or pricing structure all stamped atomically here.
- `created_at`: Snapshot creation timestamp. Supports time-travel queries and audit logs.
- `note`: Editor note, reason, or comment about why the snapshot was saved.

### `ai_mall_order_payments`

Order Payment Entity - Implements requirement from Payment Processing: stores individual payment events per order (cash/credit/point/etc), split payments, and refunds. 3NF: atomic payment events only, all aggregation handled in reporting.

Business purpose: Handles multiple payment attempts per order (installments, refunds), tracks method, amount, and status. Example: User pays half by card, half by points = 2 payment records. Key relationships: Links to ai_mall_orders, payment method, and admin (verified or managed by).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each payment record.
- `ai_mall_order_id`: Reference to order's [ai_mall_orders.id](#ai_mall_orders) - the order being paid/refunded.
- `ai_mall_admin_id`: If manually processed or confirmed, admin actor's [ai_mall_admins.id](#ai_mall_admins).
- `payment_method`: Payment Method Code - Implements business logic around payment types: card, cash, deposit, point, etc. Normalized: only short code, details in other structures or policies.
- `paid_amount`: Exact paid amount for this payment event. Normalized: no aggregation or reporting fields.
- `paid_currency`: Currency code for paid_amount (e.g., USD, KRW).
- `payment_status`: Current status of payment (e.g., pending, completed, failed). May reference future status enum/extensions.
- `payment_transaction_id`: External or gateway transaction reference ID.
- `paid_at`: Timestamp when payment was processed/received (atomic event).
- `note`: Additional comment or admin note for this payment event.
- `created_at`: Payment record creation timestamp for audit/tracing.

### `ai_mall_order_fulfillments`

Order Fulfillment Entity - Implements fulfillment tracking required for each order (shipping, delivery, pickup, etc). This is strictly normalized (3NF), with all summary data (e.g., delivery times, ship addresses) snapshotted for audit/history only.

Business purpose: Each record tracks one fulfillment event: outbound, return, partial, correction, etc. Supports multi-stage or split fulfillment. Example: 1 Order, 2 shipments. Key relationships: Links to ai_mall_orders, admin (actor), references external shipper/courier via external fields only.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique fulfillment event.
- `ai_mall_order_id`: Parent order's [ai_mall_orders.id](#ai_mall_orders) - the order being fulfilled.
- `ai_mall_admin_id`: Admin actor's [ai_mall_admins.id](#ai_mall_admins) if fulfillment was manually recorded or overseen.
- `fulfillment_type`: Type of fulfillment event (e.g., shipping, in-store pickup, return, exchange).
- `fulfilled_quantity`: Quantity fulfilled in this event (supports partial and staged fulfillments/returns).
- `external_courier_code`: External courier or logistics provider code. Implements API/data exchange compliance without denormalizing shipment info in regular tables.
- `tracking_number`: Package tracking number assigned by courier (for customer/state/reference).
- `fulfilled_at`: Timestamp when fulfillment was completed/carried out.
- `created_at`: Fulfillment record's creation timestamp for audit/history purposes.
- `memo`: Free-form comment, reason, or admin note for this fulfillment event.

### `ai_mall_order_fraud_flags`

Order Fraud Flag Entity - Implements the AI-driven fraud detection and manual override requirements from Cart & Order Processing and Analytics. 3NF is kept by storing each flag as a normalized record (not as aggregate or summary).

Business purpose: Each record is a fraud alert, risk score, or manual override for an order. Example: AI detects high risk; flag is set with score/status/reason. Key relationships: linked to ai_mall_orders, ai_mall_admins (if acted on), with timestamps and audit trail.

Special behaviors: Rigorous auditability. No denormalized metrics (counts/totals) are stored here – all reporting is handled externally or in mv_/analytics tables.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique fraud flag record.
- `ai_mall_order_id`: Order's [ai_mall_orders.id](#ai_mall_orders) that is suspected or flagged.
- `ai_mall_admin_id`: Admin's [ai_mall_admins.id](#ai_mall_admins) if flag is set/acknowledged manually.
- `flag_type`: Type of flag (e.g., ai_detected, manual, cleared, investigation).
- `risk_score`: Numerical risk score assigned by AI or manual review. Normalization: calculated values or rollups are stored only in analytics, not here.
- `status`: Current status of the fraud flag (e.g., active, resolved, dismissed).
- `reason`: Textual reason or explanation why this flag was set (free-form or code references).
- `created_at`: Flag record's creation timestamp for historical/audit compliance.

### `ai_mall_promotions`

Promotion Campaigns - Implements core promotional campaign, sale event, and discount activities from the promotions and loyalty system documentation. Keeps campaigns atomic and normalized (3NF), supporting scheduling, activation, deactivation, and analytic tracing. This table has no calculated fields and is referenced by coupons. Example use: "Summer Sale" applied across listed categories.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each promotion campaign.
- `title`: Title of the promotion event for user display. Example: 'Summer Sale'. 1NF atomic.
- `description`: Detailed description for analytics and user understanding. For example, '10% off all orders over $50'.
- `start_at`: When promotion is scheduled to begin. 3NF, atomic.
- `end_at`: When promotion is scheduled to end. 3NF, atomic.
- `active`: If this promotion is currently active. Support for dynamic toggling. 1NF atomic.
- `created_at`: Created timestamp for audit trail. 1NF atomic.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp for history trace. 1NF atomic.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete for compliance. 3NF atomic, null if not deleted.

### `ai_mall_coupons`

Coupons - Implements business requirements for code-based campaign offers as per promotions and loyalty system documentation. Supports stackable/exclusive coupon logic with enforced normalization. Example: 'WELCOME10' code for first order discount. Coupons can be linked to promotions and issued individually through coupon issuances. This model maintains referential integrity with ai_mall_promotions where 'promotion_id' is set, holding no calculated fields. 3NF compliance.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each coupon.
- `promotion_id`: Associated promotion's ai_mall_promotions.id. Links the coupon to a high-level marketing event. May be null for one-off coupons. Referential integrity to ai_mall_promotions.
- `code`: Unique coupon code for redemption (e.g., 'SUMMER2025'). 1NF atomic.
- `description`: Description of coupon offer logic. Used for customer-facing messaging and analytics.
- `type`: Coupon type, e.g. percentage/fixed/free_shipping. Used for validation logic. 1NF atomic.
- `value`: Discount value for the coupon, as per type. 1NF atomic.
- `min_purchase_amount`: Minimum spend required to activate this coupon. 3NF atomic (null if inapplicable).
- `usage_limit`: Maximum number of global redemptions for coupon (anti-abuse control). 1NF atomic.
- `per_user_limit`: Allowed usage count per user (anti-abuse control). 3NF atomic, null = unlimited.
- `valid_from`: Coupon usable from this time (for scheduling window). 1NF atomic.
- `valid_until`: Date/time coupon expires. 1NF atomic.
- `stackable`: Whether this coupon can be combined with others. 1NF atomic.
- `exclusive`: Whether coupon must be used alone (enforced exclusivity). 3NF atomic.
- `enabled`: If this coupon is currently enabled in the system (admin toggling). 1NF atomic.
- `created_at`: Created timestamp. 1NF atomic.
- `updated_at`: Updated timestamp. 1NF atomic.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete for audit/compliance. 3NF, null if not deleted.

### `ai_mall_coupon_issuances`

Coupon Issuance Records - Represents every instance where a coupon is issued/granted to a particular user for redemption tracking, audit, and analytics. 3NF-compliant. Links to coupons and users, supporting anti-abuse and compliance tracks. Example: Record for single-user coupon issued to attract new customer.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each coupon issuance instance.
- `coupon_id`: Coupon identifier (ai_mall_coupons.id). Links issuance to its coupon for validation and audit. Referential integrity enforced.
- `user_id`: Issued-to user identifier (ai_mall_customers.id, external). Required for personalized coupon assignment. Referential integrity to external users table.
- `issued_at`: When this coupon was issued. Used for redemption and audit trails. 1NF atomic.
- `expires_at`: Date/time this issued coupon expires (may differ from coupon's global expiry). 3NF atomic.
- `redeemed`: Flag for usage status. True if user redeemed, else False. 1NF atomic.
- `created_at`: Creation time (audit/compliance). 1NF atomic.
- `updated_at`: Last update time (audit/tracing). 1NF atomic.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp. 3NF atomic, null if not deleted.

### `ai_mall_coupon_usages`

Coupon Usage Records - Each user redemption of a coupon, linked to the specific issuance and the corresponding order. 3NF compliance. Maintains full audit trace for compliance and fraud prevention. Example: User redeems a coupon on checkout, record is created for exact order-coupon relationship.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each coupon usage record.
- `issuance_id`: Coupon issuance identifier (ai_mall_coupon_issuances.id) being redeemed. Referential integrity with issued coupon.
- `order_id`: Order identifier (ai_mall_orders.id, external) for which coupon applied. Referential integrity to external orders table.
- `used_at`: When the coupon was redeemed. 1NF atomic.
- `created_at`: Creation time for audit. 1NF atomic.
- `updated_at`: Update time for audit/audit trail. 1NF atomic.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp for compliance/audit. 3NF, null if not deleted.

### `ai_mall_loyalty_tiers`

Loyalty Tiers - Defines customer tier levels for the loyalty system (e.g., Silver, Gold, Platinum) as per business requirements. 3NF. No direct user-link; used in analytics and benefits assignment. Each row represents eligibility rules for a tier. Example: Gold = 10,000+ points. All keys/description fields are atomic and normalized.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key for each loyalty tier record.
- `name`: Descriptive tier name (e.g., 'Platinum'). Must be unique. 1NF atomic.
- `min_points`: Minimum point balance required to unlock this tier. 1NF atomic.
- `max_points`: Upper bound for tier (null = unlimited). Used for automated tier upgrades. 3NF atomic.
- `enabled`: Whether this tier is enabled by admin. 1NF atomic.
- `created_at`: Created timestamp. 1NF atomic.
- `updated_at`: Updated timestamp. 1NF atomic.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete for audit/compliance. 3NF, null if not deleted.

### `ai_mall_loyalty_point_ledgers`

Loyalty Point Ledgers - Tracks each instance of user loyalty point accrual/deduction for compliance, analytics, and accurate balance management. 3NF, atomic fields only. Each row is an atomic point movement, not a summary. Example: +200 for new order, -50 for redemption. Linked to user for exact balance trace. No aggregates stored.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key for each loyalty point ledger transaction.
- `user_id`: User identifier for the points transaction (ai_mall_customers.id, external). Referential integrity to users domain.
- `change_type`: Type: earn/redeem/adjust. String code for analytics and business logic. 1NF atomic.
- `amount`: Point amount (earn=positive, redeem=negative, adjust=positive/negative). 3NF atomic.
- `reason`: Explanation for business logic, e.g., 'order_placement' or 'admin_correction'. 3NF atomic, optional.
- `created_at`: Created timestamp for audit and ledgers. 1NF atomic.

### `ai_mall_deposits`

Deposit Ledger - Manages store credits and similar compensation flows for regulatory and audit compliance; each record is a normalized, atomic adjustment. Linked to user for accurate, auditable ledgers. Example: Refund as deposit credit due to return. Tracks reason, value, user only; no non-normalized/cached fields present.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key for each deposit ledger transaction.
- `user_id`: Customer account id for deposit/credit (ai_mall_customers.id, external). Referential integrity to users module.
- `change_type`: Deposit transaction reason/type (e.g., issue, refund, adjustment, compensation). 1NF atomic.
- `amount`: Amount of credit issued (can be negative if reversed). 3NF atomic.
- `reason`: Explanation string for audit trail (business logic free-text). 3NF atomic, optional.
- `created_at`: Created timestamp for audit and compliance. 1NF atomic.

### `ai_mall_point_transactions`

Point Transaction Ledger - This implements the platform's requirement for a reliable, immutable audit trail of all point-related activities as outlined in the loyalty/promotion and auditing sections of the requirements (see 05_ai-mall_promotions-and-loyalty-systems.md and 09_ai-mall_security-compliance-accessibility.md).

Tracks every accrual, redemption, or adjustment of loyalty/mileage points for any user. Maintains 3NF normalization by modeling each transaction atomically (no aggregate fields, only point deltas per event). Example: when a customer earns points from an order, or redeems points at checkout, a row is created here. Supports full historical tracing for reversals, fraud investigation, and compliance/audit purposes.

Key relationships: references user (foreign key, e.g., ai_mall_customers.id), optionally associates to order or coupon, references rule for why points were changed. Special behavior: rows are immutable for audit; reversal is modeled as a new, opposite-amount transaction.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each point transaction.
- `ai_mall_customer_id`: Belonged customer's [ai_mall_customers.id](#ai_mall_customers). The user who owns this point transaction.
- `ai_mall_point_rule_id`: Applied rule's [ai_mall_point_rules.id](#ai_mall_point_rules). The business rule (e.g., reason or campaign) under which the points were created/consumed.
- `change_type`: Type of transaction - Implements point event reason mapping. E.g., 'accrual' for earning, 'redemption' for spend, 'reversal', etc. Ensures normalization by storing atomic event type rather than embedding logic.
- `amount`: Points added/subtracted. Always positive; sign (+/-) determines addition or subtraction. Enforces atomic point changes for each event.
- `description`: Optional transaction detail for user-facing logs or admin/audit review. Maps to enhanced auditability requirement.
- `created_at`: Transaction creation timestamp. Immutable, ensures strict order and unique event log. Used for audit, chronological tracing, balance calculation.

### `ai_mall_point_rules`

Point Rule Definitions - Implements the need for flexible, traceable point accrual/redemption business logic (see 05_ai-mall_promotions-and-loyalty-systems.md).

Stores the definition and configuration of all point-related rules and campaigns (e.g., 'Earn 2 points per $1 at category X', 'Birthday bonus', 'Refund adjustment'). Maintains normalization by separating rule logic from transaction and balance. Example: each time a point action occurs, it references a rule row here (either a standard accrual, event promo, or manual adjustment).

Key relationships: referenced by point transactions. Special behaviors: rules can be activated/deactivated, may include metadata/config for automation, can be time-bounded (start/end).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each point rule.
- `rule_code`: Unique code for rule. Implements requirement for auditable, human/machine readable business identifiers (e.g., 'JOIN_BONUS2025'). 3NF: allows easy rule lookup without denormalization.
- `name`: Display name for the rule. Maps to business compliance and admin UI/analytics display requirements.
- `description`: Detailed explanation of the rule/logic (for admin/audit/UIs).
- `active`: Is the rule currently in effect? Implements enable/disable flows for promotions and regulatory compliance. 3NF: no redundancy; just binary flag.
- `start_at`: Rule effect start time. Allows time-based, scheduled point actions/promos. Nullable if always active.
- `end_at`: Rule effect end time. Nullable if open-ended or permanent rule.
- `metadata`: Optional JSON metadata for extensibility (e.g., custom rule configs, dynamic parameters).

### `ai_mall_point_balances`

Point Balances by User - Implements the requirement for instant user dashboard display of current point status (see promotions/loyalty UX guidelines). Serves as the current 'materialized' view of all point transactions, but fully normalized (not a denormalized/cached sum—actual materialized views would use 'mv_' prefix and only for reporting/performance).

Stores a user's current available (spendable) and pending (e.g., under review or lock-up) point balances. All balance changes derive exclusively from transactions (no manual updates permitted). Example: when a user earns or spends points, after successful transaction insert, this table is atomically updated. Key for customer UX, checkout validation, loyalty dashboards.

Key relationships: references ai_mall_customers (user), but does not duplicate history. Special behaviors: 1:1 with user; business rules prohibit negative available balances.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each user's balance row.
- `ai_mall_customer_id`: Belonged customer's [ai_mall_customers.id](#ai_mall_customers). One row per customer (1:1 constraint).
- `available_points`: Current available (spendable) point balance. 0 or positive integer, always derived from transaction history. No redundancy—enforces normalization.
- `pending_points`: Points pending (e.g., earned but not cleared, or locked). 0 or positive integer, never negative. Separation enables precise deduction flows, as required for order and refund handling. No aggregation/pre-calculation in this table; always normalized.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp for balance record. For concurrency control and user/account dashboard accuracy logging. Only updated on legitimate balance change event.

### `ai_mall_inquiries`

[Inquiry] Implements inquiry registration in the Interaction & Personalization requirements. Allows customers to submit questions regarding products or orders, visible to sellers and optionally admins. Maintains 3NF via FKs to customer/product/order. Example: Customer asks if a product ships internationally, seller/admin responds via comments. Key relationships: ai_mall_customers, ai_mall_products, ai_mall_orders; commented via ai_mall_inquiry_comments.

- `id`: Primary Key.

- `body`: Inquiry full content. Structurally distinct from comments. Example: 'When will this ship?'

- `created_at`: When the inquiry was created. Enables audit/chronology.
- `updated_at`: Last update. Enables audit, change tracking.

### `ai_mall_inquiry_comments`

[Inquiry Comment] Implements communication/follow-up on inquiries per requirements (threaded support, role separation). Maintains 3NF, separate from ai_mall_inquiries. Supports moderation, threading via parent_id (self-reference), and role-based authorship.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.

- `body`: Comment content. Implements threaded support content or follow-up.
- `status`: Moderation/workflow state. (e.g., 'active','hidden','deleted')
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Update timestamp for audit trail.

[Review Comment] Implements comment thread for review system (feedback, moderation, replies). Maintains linkage to review, role-based authorship, self-referencing for threading.

### `ai_mall_articles`

Article entity - This implements the platform article/post requirement for news, blog content, or editorial material. Articles serve as informational or promotional content authored by admins (or sellers, if permitted). Each article can have multiple comments and be assigned to one or more article categories. Fully normalized by separating main article data, comments, and category mappings. For example, an admin can publish new feature updates, or a seller can post promotional articles. Key relationships: references to authors (admin or seller), links to category and comments. Special behaviors: articles can be edited or unpublished but retain audit trail via snapshots if needed.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each article.
- `author_admin_id`: Reference to admin author's [ai_mall_admins.id](#ai_mall_admins). Indicates article is authored by an admin. Nullable if authored by seller.
- `author_seller_id`: Reference to seller author's [ai_mall_sellers.id](#ai_mall_sellers). Indicates article is authored by a seller. Nullable if authored by admin.
- `category_id`: Assigned article category's [ai_mall_article_categories.id](#ai_mall_article_categories). Categorizes article for navigation, filtering, or display/grouping.
- `title`: Title of the article - Implements the requirement for article headline. Main descriptor for search, display, and navigation. Fully atomic and required.
- `slug`: SEO-friendly slug/URL segment for the article. Used for human-readable and indexable links. Example: 'ai-mall-launch-event'. Ensures normalization by separating from title/body.
- `body`: Main content body - Implements article textual/HTML content as fully normalized field. No derived or summary fields included. For example, product launch details, guides, etc.
- `published`: Publication flag - Indicates whether article is publicly visible or in draft/unpublished state. Implements content moderation flow. Not calculated; atomic status only.
- `pinned`: Pinned flag for featured or promoted articles. Atomic flag (true if highlighted), maintains fully normalized structure.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp for the article. Atomic event time, not derived. Enforces audit trail requirements.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp for the article. Used for audit and change tracking per non-functional requirements. Not calculated.

### `ai_mall_article_comments`

Article comment entity - Implements the ability for users to comment on articles as per interaction and personalization requirements. Allows multiple comments per article, supports threaded/hierarchical replies via parent_id. Maintains 3NF by separating comment text, article association, and user identity. Usage example: customers, sellers, or admins can add discussion/comments on news, guides, etc. Key relationships: links to article, parent (for threads), and comment author (customer, seller, or admin). Special behaviors: moderation, visibility, and deletion handled at application layer.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each comment.
- `article_id`: Reference to parent article's [ai_mall_articles.id](#ai_mall_articles). Each comment belongs to one article.
- `author_customer_id`: Reference to commenting customer's [ai_mall_customers.id](#ai_mall_customers), if comment was left by a customer. Nullable if comment by seller/admin.
- `author_seller_id`: Reference to commenting seller's [ai_mall_sellers.id](#ai_mall_sellers), if comment was left by a seller. Nullable if comment by customer/admin.
- `author_admin_id`: Reference to commenting admin's [ai_mall_admins.id](#ai_mall_admins), if comment was left by an admin. Nullable if comment by customer/seller.
- `parent_id`: Optional self-reference to parent comment ([ai_mall_article_comments.id](#ai_mall_article_comments)) for threaded discussions. Null for top-level comments, set for replies.
- `body`: Main comment text body - Implements atomic requirement to store actual user comment content. Fully normalized; no derived sentiment or summary fields. For example: customer leaves question, seller provides answer.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp - Meets audit/auditability requirement for comment event. Not calculated.
- `updated_at`: Last edit timestamp for the comment. Supports moderation and edit trail functionality per requirements.

### `ai_mall_article_categories`

Article category entity - Implements requirement for grouping articles for organization, navigation, filtering, and SEO. Maintains 3NF by separating categorical metadata from articles. For example, guides, news, policy updates, etc. Each category can be assigned to multiple articles. Hierarchy (parent-child) allows nesting categories. Special behaviors: if parent_id is set, forms category tree; else is a root-level category. Application can enforce business logic on parent/child constraints.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each article category.
- `parent_id`: Optional parent category's [ai_mall_article_categories.id](#ai_mall_article_categories) for category hierarchy and nesting. Null for root categories.
- `name`: Category name - Implements the requirement for unique, human-readable article category label. Ensures normalization.
- `slug`: SEO-friendly category slug for URLs/navigation. Must be unique within categories. Example: 'news-updates'. Maintains normalization by not duplicating category name.
- `description`: Optional category description - Implements meta/SEO or UI tooltip requirement. Nullable, not required.

### `ai_mall_analytics_events`

Analytics Event Entity - This implements the requirements for tracking distinct analytics events as demanded in the advanced analytics and AI documentation. 

Business explanation: Each row represents a single captured analytics event (click, page view, purchase, search, error) generated by any user or system process. Maintains 3NF compliance—event details and context are atomic and not derived. For example, when a customer adds an item to their cart, a new analytics event is created referencing its type and holding contextual payload (serialized JSON). 

Key relationships: Ties to ai_mall_analytics_event_types for type definition, can reference actor tables (not directly modeled here). 
Special behaviors: Loosely coupled with user/session IDs for flexibility; all business logic for attribution is handled externally.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each analytics event record.
- `event_type_id`: Event type reference - Links to event type definition in [ai_mall_analytics_event_types.id](#ai_mall_analytics_event_types) to ensure event categorization adheres to system-defined taxonomy. Relationship is required for classification.
- `occurred_at`: Event Occurrence Timestamp - Implements the requirement to record the exact UTC time of the event occurrence. Maintains strict normalization with explicit, unambiguous timestamps. For example, used for all time-based analytics, daily active users, or sequence analysis.
- `actor_id`: Actor Reference (Loose/Flexible) - Optionally associates an event with any system actor (customer, seller, admin). Implements the requirement for user attribution analytics (inferred by external joins). Maintains normalization by not duplicating user state; can be null for system/bot events.
- `session_id`: Session Reference (Loose/Flexible) - Optionally attributes the event to a browsing session or device identity for anonymous event tracking. Enforces normalization by keeping only the session UUID here; session metadata is external.
- `context_payload`: Contextual Event Data (JSON/String) - Stores serialized event context payload (click details, product IDs, metadata) as a JSON string field for semi-structured extensibility. Ensures normalization by never repeating structured relations; payload structure is externally enforced. Example: '{"productId": "abc-123", "action": "add_to_cart", "value": 8990 }'.
- `ip_address`: IP Address - Implements the requirement to optionally log origin IP for risk or source analysis. Ensures atomicity by storing only address string. Usage: geo-analytics, fraud investigations, etc.

### `ai_mall_analytics_event_types`

Analytics Event Type Entity - Implements cataloging all event types (category, action codes) as defined in the advanced analytics system requirements. 

Business purpose: Each entry defines a logical type of analytics event such as 'page_view', 'add_to_cart', 'purchase', 'error', etc. Maintains 3NF by separating event occurrence from event taxonomy. For example, when a new event type such as 'wishlist_add' is required, it's created here and referenced by all relevant event records. 

Key relationships: Referenced by events; not directly tied to user/session. 
Special behaviors: Type codes and human-readable names must be unique; descriptions provide API and analytics clarity.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for event type definition.
- `code`: Event Type Code - Implements code-based requirement for system-wide event type consistency (e.g., 'page_view', 'add_to_cart'). Must be unique. Maintains normalization by de-coupling event occurrence from type metadata. Example: Used in analytics queries for grouping.
- `name`: Event Type Name - Implements requirement for human-readable descriptive name for event type. Example: 'Page View', 'Cart Add'. Supports admin-facing analytics UI lookup.
- `description`: Event Type Description - Implements requirement for extended explanation, API tooltip, or audit notes. Maintains normalization by attaching only to type, not to each event.

### `ai_mall_user_dashboards`

User Dashboard Configuration Entity - Implements requirement to let each user (actor) configure personal analytics dashboards as described in analytics and personalization documentation. 

Business purpose: Each record stores dashboard configuration for a specific user—what widgets or reports are pinned, layout configuration as JSON, and timestamps. Maintains 3NF with atomic user association and configuration payload. Used to persist user dashboard state across sessions and devices.

Key relationships: References actor ID (can be customer, seller, or admin - stored as UUID; resolving the actual actor is external).
Special behaviors: One dashboard config per actor (enforced by unique index); supports time-based filtering and historical layout snapshots.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each dashboard configuration.
- `actor_id`: Actor/User Reference - Attributed to a user (any actor type) via system UUID. Ensures every dashboard belongs to exactly one user; resolving actual user is handled in application logic. Not nullable.
- `dashboard_payload`: Dashboard Configuration Payload - Implements storage of widget/report configuration as serialized JSON. Maintains strict normalization as atomic config blob only; no duplicated data. Example: '{"widgets": ["sales_chart", "visits_map"]}'.
- `created_at`: Dashboard Created Timestamp - Date/time of configuration creation. Ensures atomic record for audit trail. Used for query, filtering, and sorting.
- `updated_at`: Dashboard Updated Timestamp - Last modification time of dashboard. Ensures traceability of configuration changes and auditability.

### `ai_mall_campaign_metrics`

Campaign Analytics Metrics Entity - Implements requirements for campaign/promotion performance measurement as required by the promotions and analytics documentation. 

Business purpose: Each row aggregates or stores campaign metrics (impressions, clicks, redemption counts, revenue, cost, ROI) for a specific campaign and date/time bucket. 
Maintains 3NF—metrics are always external/per campaign/per period, never pre-calculated totals. Used by seller/admin dashboards and reporting tools.

Key relationships: References campaign or promotion via UUID (campaign table external to this domain, relationship by UUID only).
Special behaviors: Metric records are independent and domain-normalized—never cache/copy derived aggregates. Composite uniqueness enforced by (campaign_id, period_start).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for campaign metric row.
- `campaign_id`: Marketing Campaign/Promotion Reference - Associates metric row to a logical campaign/promotion/offer (defined externally). UUID only; campaign metadata resolved externally. Not nullable.
- `period_start`: Metrics Period Start - Implements reporting granularity (e.g., daily, hourly) for time series analytics. Enforces normalization with explicit period-bucketed data only. Used in charts and time-based queries.
- `impressions`: Impressions Count - Implements raw metric requirement for number of times campaign was displayed. Atomic count (not accumulated). Maintains normalization as primitive numeric fact only.
- `clicks`: Clicks Count - Implements requirement to store number of user clicks on the campaign. Atomic, fully normalized field, not a calculation.
- `redemptions`: Redemptions Count - Requirement to track coupon/promotion redemption count. Maintains atomic normalization.
- `revenue`: Revenue Attributed - Requirement for revenue measurement attributed to campaign. Maintains strict normalization as atomic recorded value (never a calculation or cache).
- `cost`: Cost Attributed - Requirement for cost metric (discounts, spend) attributed to campaign. Stored as atomic numeric value (never as a calculated or derived field).
- `roi`: ROI - Implements requirement to persist measured return on investment for the specific campaign/time. Must be atomic and calculated externally; never duplicated/derived in reporting queries.
